newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Belgians can get 32-hour week with salary loss.
newsitem.headline: Belgians can get 32-hour week with salary loss.

text.p: The Belgian government has created the possibility for large companies to cut the working week to 32 hours from 38 hours with reduced wages for workers, the budget ministry said on Monday.
A ministry spokesman told Reuters the measure was part of a package to create jobs through the redistribution of labour and by making the labour market more flexible.

The 32-hour week can be applied only in companies employing more than 50 people, and on condition that employers and workers agree on this in the works council and that the employer's total wage costs do not increase.
"The total salary mass (within a company) must remain unchanged," he said.
He said it was unclear how many jobs this could create as the new system is entirely on a voluntary basis.

Another key measure is that people who have been unemployed for more than five years can keep their unemployment benefits if they are for service jobs. In that case, the employer will only pay a small extra sum on top of the benefits.
The new scheme is targeted to create more jobs in functions which require little education, such as petrol pump attendants and recycling empty bottles in supermarkets.
"The idea is to reintegrate these people in the labour process and to fill a need for services in society which otherwise are not fulfilled," he said.
A specific list with the kinds of jobs which will be applicable for the scheme will be drawn up.
There are about 85,000 people in Belgium who have been unemployed for more than five years. At the end of February, Belgium had 571,660 registered unemployed, or 13.4 of the workforce.

Among other measures, the government will also extend to the end of 1998 the period during which employers can offer renewable, time-limited labour contracts. This allows employers to keep an employee on trial for a longer time. Many employers refuse to hire as firing costs in Belgium are high.
-- Geert De Clercq, Brussels Newsroom +32 2 287 6813, Fax +32 2 230 7710
